chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says to his believing brother, 'Welcome!', Allah the Exalted writes for him a 'Welcome' until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.لِأَخِيهِ الْمُؤْمِنِ: To his believing brother (referring to a fellow Muslim)
key_terms.مَرْحَباً: Welcome (a term of greeting and hospitality)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for greeting a Muslim brother warmly?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to highlight the spiritual weight of social etiquette (*adab*) within the Shia community, where a simple greeting is not merely polite but a divinely recorded act of worship. The repetition of 'Marhaban' signifies a reciprocal divine welcome, underscoring the concept of *Mu'akhat* (brotherhood) as a tangible means of accumulating merit (*hasanat*) that persists until the Hereafter. This reflects the Shia emphasis on honoring the believer (*Ta'zim al-Mu'min*) as a core component of faith.
